reviewFindings.title: Preserve the cancellation signal when draining queued requests
reviewFindings.body: The new signal is stored on the task, but service.drain still calls execute({ input: task.input }, transport), discarding it. With the default queued: true, submitting a request, aborting its signal, and then draining invokes transport instead of rejecting without execution. Aborting after execution starts also cannot reach the transport because it receives signal: undefined. Pass the complete task through the drain adapter so both paths use the worker's cancellation handling.

result.solutionAssessment: The worker is an appropriate shared owner for the abort check, and the queue already isolates rejected jobs, but the service adapter must preserve the signal for the change to work across both entrypoints.

reviewFindings.title: Preserve the AbortSignal when draining queued tasks
reviewFindings.body: Queued submissions store the new signal, but drain still calls execute({ input: task.input }, transport), dropping it. For example, submit "report-42" with a signal, abort its controller, then call drain: execute sees no signal and invokes transport instead of rejecting. Signals are also never forwarded for cancellation after queued work starts. Since queued execution is the default, the advertised feature fails on the normal path. Pass the complete task to execute from the drain callback.

result.solutionAssessment: Centralizing pre-execution cancellation and transport forwarding in execute is appropriate, but the queued path must preserve the task rather than reconstructing only its input.
